messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 Pager: High error rate observed for customer AvaPharma (dedicated pool df-ava-1). 503s and increased tail latency. Alert threshold: 3% errors over 5m. Link: https://observability/redwood/df-ava-1

maria: Seeing it on dashboards too — canary traffic to artifact `redwood-runtime:release-2027f` spiking. 95th pct latency jumped to ~1.2s from 180ms. 5xxs mainly `kv cache miss -> OOM-ish` in logs.

devon: Confirmed. Repro locally against canary node, saw repeated `gpu oom` in runtime logs when sequence len > 1024. Might be a kernel/regression in the new build.

kevin-runtime: @devon can you paste the exact error lines? I want to check the kernel selector path.

devon: log snippet: ```
[2026-03-12T15:34:10Z] ERROR runtime: kv_cache_set failed: out of memory (alloc 128MB)
[2026-03-12T15:34:10Z] WARN request 0x7f3a: falling back to unbatched path -> high latency
[2026-03-12T15:34:11Z] ERROR serve: response error: 503 downstream error
```

maria: Customer impact: ~6% of AvaPharma requests failing in canary cohort (10% of their traffic). Their SLA load tests are running right now. Lia, heads-up to customer?

lia-cse: On it. Drafting a brief: "We observed elevated errors for a subset of traffic in your dedicated pool; we're actively rolling back the canary and will update you in 15m." Will post to their dedicated Slack and set expectations.

devon: Proposed mitigation: pin df-ava-1 to previous artifact `release-2027c` and divert canary traffic back. Steps: 1) set pin, 2) scale pool to absorb revert traffic briefly, 3) monitor heatmap. Anyone object?

ops-lead: +1, prioritize rollback. Keep canary cohort isolated until we root cause.

kevin-runtime: If pin command is straightforward, I can run it. Also want to capture a heap of the failing node first. Commands: ```
# capture logs & heap
redwood infra ssh df-ava-1-canary-02 -- 'sudo /opt/redwood/bin/dump_heap.sh /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).prof'
# set pinned artifact
redwoodctl pools pin-artifact df-ava-1 --artifact redwood-runtime:release-2027c --reason "canary regressions 2026-03-12"
```

deploy-bot: Deployment event queued: pin request for df-ava-1 by kevin-runtime. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/pin-artifact

kevin-runtime: Running the heap dump now, then running pin command. Will post back when complete.

oncall-sre: Handing off incident lead to @kevin-runtime. I'll stay in loop for escalation.

kevin-runtime: Pin command applied. Output: ```
INFO: pool df-ava-1 pinned to redwood-runtime:release-2027c
INFO: routing updated: canary cohort -> legacy routing
```

maria: I see error rate falling in the last 2m; 5xxs back down to ~0.4%, latency 95th ~200ms. Nice.

lia-cse: Sent update to AvaPharma: "We've rolled back canary to the previous runtime and are seeing errors decline. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline for a safe redeploy." They replied: "Thanks — please share RCA asap, tests are sensitive."

devon: Captured heap + logs uploaded to /artifacts/incidents/2072103456/ — saved core of canary node and perf traces, also took kernel selection trace.

ops-lead: Great. Immediate mitigation successful. Next actions: 1) full root-cause analysis (runtime regression suspected), 2) block release-2027f from other pools until patch, 3) coordinate controlled repro & test harness. Assign owners?

kevin-runtime: I'll own rollback validation & kernel-selector bisect with @devon. Target: reproduce in lab and build a minimal test that exercises the kv cache path. ETA 48h.

maria: Lia will coordinate customer comms. Ops to file block on release artifact: `release-2027f` flagged.

oncall-sre: I'll close the pager as mitigated but keep monitoring alerts for 2h.

incident-bot: Incident status changed -> mitigated. Severity: SEV3 -> monitoring. Incident link: https://incidents.redwood/2072103456

maria: Thanks everyone. We'll schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow and add follow-ups to the incident ticket.

kevin-runtime: Logged action items: ["bisect kernel change", "add kv-cache e2e test with seq len >1024", "block artifact 2027f"]. I'll update ticket when bisect starts.

lia-cse: Customer happy with rollback update. Keeping them in watchers for the postmortem.

ops-lead: Nice fast coordination. Closing thread once the postmortem is scheduled. :thumbsup:
